correctness.rationale: Exchangeability conditional on K=r makes each r-set equally likely, yielding the directed k-chord inclusion probability binom(n−k−1,r−2)/binom(n,r). The perimeter expectation is 2R Σ_k w_k Σ_i sin(S_i,k/2), including the doubled-edge convention for two retained points. Jensen strict concavity on (0,2π) gives the regular unique maximum because w1>0 whenever survival of two vertices has positive probability. A second-order Taylor expansion and normalized DFT Parseval give the full Hessian Λ_mode; the k=1 term makes every nonconstant mode strictly positive. Bernoulli weights p²(1−p)^{k−1} telescope by complex geometric series. An independently enumerated five-vertex Bernoulli example at p=0.37,R=1.8 agrees with the formula to 1e−15; the proof, not enumeration, covers arbitrary n and exchangeable laws.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Madras–KC compute uniform subconfiguration perimeters of an already regular polygon; Morin samples independent interior points, and Reitzner–Schütt–Werner sample from continuous polytope boundaries. None of those inspected models optimizes arbitrary cyclic angular configurations with fully exchangeable thinning and reports the discrete-Fourier curvature spectrum.

value.rationale: Simultaneously optimizing geometry under arbitrary exchangeable failures is a natural stochastic-design problem, and identifying every Fourier sensitivity mode quantifies robustness of the optimal regular polygon. The exact Bernoulli formula and strictness are useful finite design facts; they do not assert global finite-deformation stability.

limitations: Older symmetric-chord-sum/Fejes-Tóth extremal theorems might already imply the global optimizer; exact all-law Fourier sensitivity still needs independent priority comparison.
